sections.h2: Which Orange County office do I call about my tax bill?
sections.html:
Orange County divides the job three ways, so the right call depends on the problem. A wrong value or missing exemption belongs to the Property Appraiser at 200 S Orange Ave, Suite 1700 in Orlando. A bill, a payment or a delinquency belongs to the Tax Collector. The rate itself is a product of local boards.

  • Value, ownership, legal description and mailing address: Property Appraiser
  • Millage: the county commission, school board, cities and special districts
  • Statements, payment plans, certificates: Tax Collector

The Tax Collector's own page says it passes the money on to 63 taxing authorities. Items such as streetlights, sewers and road work are non-ad valorem charges, priced per unit and printed on the same statement.

sections.h2: What is the Orange County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Value is fixed on January 1, bills reach owners by the first of November, and the whole balance has to be in the Tax Collector's hands before April begins.

Orange County property tax calendar from the Tax Collector and the state revenue department
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Last day to file an exemption request
AugustProposed tax notice mailed
By November 1Statements mailed
November to FebruaryFour, three, two and one percent discounts
March 31Gross amount and deferral applications due
April 1Delinquency begins
By June 1Online certificate sale

A check postmarked March 30 but delivered in April is late, because the office goes by receipt.

sections.h2: How much can an early payment save in Orange County?
sections.html:
Pay in November and the bill drops four percent. Each month after that trims one point less, ending at one percent in February, and March pays the gross figure.

Sellers who close in winter can pay the whole year at the closing table, so the month on the contract changes the net. Ask your title agent for the figure that matches your closing date. If a lender pays from escrow, it can request the statement, and you get a copy labeled as requested by the lender; do not pay twice.

Owners who are current and whose prior bill topped $100 can ask for the quarterly installment plan, which is applied for online at the Tax Collector's site.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to a home in Orange County?
sections.html:
Homestead leads the list, and the Property Appraiser says it can lower taxable value by as much as $50,000. In the state's description, the opening $25,000 touches every levy, and a second slice reaches only non-school levies above $50,000 of assessed value.

File with the Property Appraiser before March 1, and live in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Widow, disability, senior and military exemptions also exist. Once homesteaded, the assessed figure may rise each year by no more than the smaller of 3 percent or the inflation change. A sale wipes out that gap on the following January 1, so a buyer's first bill can be well above yours. The Property Appraiser's tax estimator is aimed at people weighing a purchase or sale.

sections.h2: What if I owe back taxes on my Orange County house?
sections.html:
You can still sell. The title agent requests a payoff from the Tax Collector, and every open balance gets cleared as part of closing.

Once April arrives, the Tax Collector adds a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost. Parcels are listed in a local paper for three straight weeks, then certificates go up for competitive bids that start at 18 percent and drop. To clear a certificate, pay the tax, accrued interest and advertising cost. Late payers must use certified or cashier's funds, a money order, certain attorney, title or escrow checks, or cash at the counter; personal and business checks are refused.

  • Ask for the payoff before you list
  • Confirm whether a certificate already exists
  • Compare escrow records with the county account

sections.h2: How long before a certificate threatens the house?
sections.html:
Two years. Only then can the certificate holder apply for a tax deed, and the Tax Collector says Orange County routes those sales through the Comptroller's Office.

Before that, state law bars the holder from pressing the owner for payment. Homestead land gets one more cushion, because the opening bid must include half of its latest assessed value on top of the money due. Even so, an owner facing this stage should call the Tax Collector's property tax department early and ask for a redemption total.

sections.h2: Can I defer homestead tax in Orange County?
sections.html:
Qualifying homesteaders can postpone part of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector before April. This is a different program from the exemption.

Postponed tax stays attached to the home as a lien, so a seller should ask the Tax Collector how a postponed balance and its interest are settled at closing. The state ties the amount to household income and lets a permanent resident aged 65 or older defer the share above 3 percent of that income.

sections.h2: Do landlords owe a second tax in Orange County?
sections.html:
Yes, if the rental holds furniture, fixtures or equipment. The Tax Collector describes tangible personal property tax as a levy on those items in businesses and rental property, and on structural additions to mobile homes.

These statements arrive alongside the real estate statements and carry the same discounts. After March 31 interest of 1.5 percent a month runs, and a collection firm under contract adds 15 percent on accounts left unpaid. Selling a furnished rental means asking the Tax Collector how any open account is handled.

sections.h2: What do Orange County numbers say about owners?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 1,528,002 people in July 2025, spread over 527,776 households. Over half of the homes are owner lived, with a middle value of $390,100. Owners with a loan pay a median $2,055 a month, and renters pay a median $1,775.

A statement's lines shift with the home's location: inside a city, in unincorporated Orange County, or within a special district. Read those lines on your own account before quoting a tax figure to a buyer.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Orange County property tax without penalty?
faqs.a: March 31, counted by the day the Tax Collector receives it. A check that lands in April is delinquent.

faqs.q: What does a November payment save?
faqs.a: Four percent. The discount shrinks by a point each month until February, and March has none.

faqs.q: Which Orange County office fixes a wrong value or missing exemption?
faqs.a: The Property Appraiser. The Tax Collector bills what the certified roll shows and cannot change value, ownership or exemptions.

faqs.q: Can a homeowner with unpaid taxes still sell in Orange County?
faqs.a: Yes. Request the Tax Collector's payoff, then let the title agent settle it at closing, with certified funds if the bill is already delinquent.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate transfer my house to an investor?
faqs.a: No. It is a lien, and you can redeem it by paying the tax, interest and advertising cost. A tax deed application cannot come until two years have passed.
